newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK 97 FX POLICY WILL SET NO DRACHMA VOL GOAL - DAILY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK 97 FX POLICY WILL SET NO DRACHMA VOL GOAL - DAILY.

text.p: The Greek government and the central bank have decided against setting a volatility target for drachma in 1997, said daily Imerisia on Wednesday.
The report was cited earleir by a trader as a reason for a firmer ecu/drachma. Ecu/drachma was trading around 304.20/30 at 1330 local (1130 GMT).

Bank of Greece has adopted the so called 'hard drachma' policy in the last few years which aims at combatting inflation by letting the drachma slide against some major european currencies, mainly the ecu, by less than justified by inflation differentials between Greece and its major trading partners.
The ecu/drachma has been used as a yardstick and the central bank managed to contain the drachma's depreciation against the ecu at 1.0 percent in 1996 and 3.0 percent in 1996.
The central bank is not expected to set an explicit ecu/drachma target for 1997 to avoid inviting speculative forex inflows and boost liquidity that might endanger its crusade against inflation.
Central bank officials have said that they favour a more volatile ecu/drachma in 1997 to discourage speculative inflows.

The central bank is also expected to cut its intervention interventio rates gradually in line with developments on the fiscal front, inflation, money supply, the drachma and the course of interest rates on some major european currencies.
It is also expect to make use of repo operations to smooth out interbank liquidity.
Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos is expected to announce the 1997 monetary policy in late January.
